title: Amphawa–Mae Klong 2-Day Cafe Trip — Riverside Coffee Route | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 2-day, 1-night cafe trip through Amphawa and Mae Klong in Samut Songkhram, Thailand. A waterfront coffee route along the canals and the Mae Klong River — real open cafes, opening hours, rough prices, and the right timing to hit them.
keywords: Amphawa cafes, Mae Klong riverside cafe, Samut Songkhram itinerary, canalside cafe Amphawa, 2-day cafe trip Thailand
intro: Amphawa and Mae Klong sit just over an hour from Bangkok, but they feel like a slower gear of life. Tides slide up and down the canals, paddle boats drift past the shopfronts, and the coffee is made with real care. This is a 2-day, 1-night plan for anyone who wants to settle into riverside cafes and actually enjoy them. We've built the route around the tides and the light, every cafe here is open right now, and we've noted opening hours and rough prices so it's easy to plan.

blocks.html: The whole appeal of cafe-hopping in Amphawa and Mae Klong is that nearly every spot hugs the water. Some sit right on a small canal where paddle boats glide by, others look out over the wide Mae Klong River and catch the full sunset in the evening. So we've set up the first day to start with the in-town Mae Klong cafes in the late morning and end by the river at dusk, then save the canal zone around Amphawa and Tha Kha — where you really want to watch the tide — for the second day.

blocks.title: Before you set off
blocks.html: Check the Mae Klong tide table ahead of time. A lot of the canalside cafes look their best at high tide, when the canal is full and paddle boats can pass through. The Amphawa Floating Market only really comes alive on Friday to Sunday evenings — if you come on a weekday it's quieter, but that also makes the cafes a lot more relaxed.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Mae Klong town cafes to the riverside at dusk

blocks.html: The first day starts in Mae Klong town, because the bakeries and specialty coffee spots are clustered around here. Leave Bangkok and you'll arrive in the late morning, right about when the shops open, then ease into the riverside zone through the late afternoon into the evening.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Mae Klong · specialty coffee to sunset

items.activity: Leave Bangkok, head for Mae Klong
items.note: Drive the Thonburi–Pak Tho route, about 1.5 hours. No car? Catch a Bangkok–Mae Klong minivan from Sai Tai Mai (Southern Bus Terminal).

items.activity: Start the morning at Bueno Dia Mae Klong
items.note: A bakery cafe in Mae Klong town known for fresh-baked sourdough and specialty coffee. It's small and warm, a good place to start the day with something light. Coffee runs about ฿70–110.

items.activity: Grab lunch in Mae Klong Market
items.note: Mae Klong Market is full of local food — Mae Klong mackerel, noodles, coconut-milk sweets. Fuel up before the next round of cafes.

items.activity: Settle in at Sutha Cafe by the Mae Klong River
items.note: A vintage riverside cafe with a cozy feel, drinks and snacks both on offer. A chill spot to work or read through the afternoon.

items.activity: Move to Phawanawa Cafe & Bistro for sunset
items.note: A riverside spot near the Amphawa Floating Market with a wide-open view and lovely evening light. Live music on Saturday and Sunday. Order a cold drink and watch the sky change color.

items.activity: Check in at a riverside stay and relax
items.note: Pick a homestay or canalside resort around Amphawa. If it's Friday to Sunday, walk the Amphawa Floating Market in the evening or take a firefly boat tour.

blocks.title: Day-one tip
blocks.html: Small bakeries like Bueno Dia sell out of their popular items fast. If you want the sourdough or a pretzel, go in the late morning before noon — don't wait until the afternoon, because they're usually gone by then.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Amphawa canal, pomelo orchards, and Tha Kha

blocks.html: Day two leans fully into the canal and orchard side of things. Start with a cafe set inside a fruit orchard — one of Mae Klong's signatures — then finish at the Tha Kha Floating Market, which is quieter and more old-school than Amphawa's. There are canalside coffee spots where you can sit with your feet dangling over the water and watch everyday village life go by.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Canalside · orchard cafes · Tha Kha Floating Market

items.activity: Breakfast at your stay, pack up
items.note: No need to rush on the second morning. Give yourself time to sip a coffee by the canal at your place before heading out.

items.activity: The Pomelo Amphawa — a cafe in a pomelo orchard
items.note: A cafe and restaurant on the Mae Klong River with its own pomelo and lychee orchards, plus indoor and outdoor seating. Pet friendly. The standouts are the desserts and drinks made from local pomelo.

items.activity: Stop by Mangrove Cafe at Tree Tara
items.note: A cafe tucked into a shady mangrove setting by the water, with coffee, homemade cake, and savory dishes like sea bass steak. A good spot for a light lunch in the shade.

items.activity: Nitan Coffee at the Tha Kha Floating Market
items.note: A bamboo-hut coffee stand on the Tha Kha canal — sit with your feet over the edge and watch the paddle boats and community life. Coffee, tea, cocoa, and fruit juices. Open Mon–Fri 09:30–17:30, Sat–Sun 08:00–18:00.

items.activity: Wander the Tha Kha Floating Market, pick up some gifts
items.note: Tha Kha is only busy on certain days, set by the tidal calendar, but the canalside shops and local goods like coconut sugar are there to take home.

items.activity: One last photo by the canal, then back to Bangkok
items.note: Leave before nightfall and you'll be back in Bangkok at a reasonable hour. If you'd rather stay another night for the Amphawa fireflies, it's worth it.

blocks.text: The riverside cafes we picked for this route

blocks.html: If you'd rather build your own route, here are the cafes we've checked are still open, sorted by style and what they do best. Pick the ones that fit your days and the tide. Prices are rough ranges and may shift with the menu.

items.name: The Pomelo Amphawa (Khrua Som-O Wan)
items.blurb: A cafe and restaurant on the Mae Klong River with its own pomelo and lychee orchards, plus indoor and outdoor seating. Pet friendly. The drinks and desserts made from pomelo are the draw.

items.name: Nitan Coffee (Tha Kha Floating Market)
items.blurb: A bamboo-hut coffee spot on the Tha Kha canal where you sit with your feet over the edge and watch the paddle boats and old-fashioned community life. Coffee, tea, cocoa, and fruit juices. Simple but full of charm.

items.name: Bueno Dia Mae Klong
items.blurb: A bakery cafe in Mae Klong town known for sourdough and bread baked fresh daily, paired with specialty coffee. Small and warm, a good place to start the morning with something light.

items.name: Sutha Cafe
items.blurb: A vintage cafe on the Mae Klong River with a cozy feel, serving both drinks and snacks. A quiet corner to work or read in the afternoon.

items.name: Phawanawa Cafe & Bistro
items.blurb: A restaurant and cafe on the river near the Amphawa Floating Market, with a wide-open view and a beautiful sunset. Live music on Saturday and Sunday. Good for a long, relaxed evening.

items.name: Mangrove Cafe @ Tree Tara
items.blurb: A cafe in a shady mangrove setting by the water, with organic coffee, homemade cake, and savory dishes like sea bass steak. Good for escaping the heat at lunchtime.

items.name: Pava Cafe & Restaurant
items.blurb: A red-brick loft-style cafe with a vintage touch out on the Thonburi–Pak Tho side of Amphawa, serving quality coffee, homemade sweets, and food. Plenty of photo corners.

items.name: The cafe at Asita Eco Resort
items.blurb: A cafe inside an eco resort on the canal, with a shady, natural feel near the Amphawa Floating Market. It leans on local ingredients and makes for a calm, uncrowded place to sit.

blocks.text: Getting there and getting the timing right

items: Driving yourself is easiest — the cafes are spread out along the canals and the river, and some are down deep side lanes. A private or rental car lets you hit several in one day.
You can come without a car — take a Bangkok–Mae Klong minivan from Sai Tai Mai (Southern Bus Terminal), about 1.5 hours, then hop on a motorbike taxi or charter a local songthaew.
Watch the tide — the canalside cafes are prettiest at high tide. At low tide the canal goes shallow and muddy, so put the canalside spots on your high-tide window to get the full atmosphere.

Weekdays and weekends are different — the Amphawa Floating Market buzzes on Friday to Sunday evenings. If you're after quiet cafes and easy photos, a weekday is better — just check that the spots you want are open that day.

blocks.title: The honest version
blocks.html: A lot of these riverside cafes are small family-run places, and their open days and menus can shift with the season and the tides. Before you head out, give them a quick call or check their page for that day so you don't make the trip for nothing — especially the ones deep along the canal.

faq.q: How many days do you need for an Amphawa–Mae Klong cafe trip?
faq.a: Two days and one night is just right. Day one works through the in-town Mae Klong cafes and the river at sunset, and day two heads into the Amphawa canal zone and the Tha Kha Floating Market. If you only have a single day, pick 3–4 cafes along one route and you'll still have a good time.

faq.q: When do the Mae Klong riverside cafes look their best?
faq.a: At high tide the canal fills up and paddle boats can pass through, so the canalside scenery is at its best. The Mae Klong River spots like Phawanawa are loveliest in the evening for the sunset. Check the tide table before you plan.

faq.q: Can you visit these cafes without your own car?
faq.a: Yes. Take a Bangkok–Mae Klong minivan from Sai Tai Mai (Southern Bus Terminal), about an hour and a half, then continue by motorbike taxi or a chartered local songthaew. But if you want to reach several cafes deep along the canal in one day, driving yourself or renting a car is much smoother.

faq.q: Is there a big difference between weekdays and weekends?
faq.a: Quite a bit. On Friday-to-Sunday weekends the Amphawa Floating Market is lively and the cafes get crowded, while weekdays are quieter, more relaxed to sit in, and easier for photos. But some shops close on weekdays, so check the open days of the spots you want first.

faq.q: Are the cafes around Amphawa–Mae Klong expensive?
faq.a: Most are easy on the wallet. Drinks start around ฿45–90 at the small canalside shops, while the riverside spots with a view and food run about ฿80–150 a glass. That's fair for the waterfront setting you get.
